title: Computational two-photon microscopy for deep tissue imaging
text:
The program aims to develop novel intravital two-photon microscopy techniques with scattering correction for
deep tissue imaging. By jointly developing optical hardware and computational software, the proposed
techniques will correct dynamic tissue scattering with high-speed, high-efficiency light modulation. This program
will offer a timely and reliable solution for imaging intact tissues and organs, catalyzing a broad range of
fundamental biological research, including the imaging of nervous systems, immune responses, embryo
development, and cancer metastasis.

title: Optimizing genetic risk models for primary open-angle glaucoma through expanded population genomic analysis
text: Primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG) is a leading cause of permanent vision loss worldwide. This project will strengthen genetic risk prediction models for POAG by incorporating large-scale datasets that capture broader genomic variation, enabling earlier identification of individuals at elevated risk for POAG. This work supports the use of precision tools to improve clinical decision-making, advance public health efforts in early disease detection and management, and ultimately help prevent blindness.

title: ADAR1 PTM in Cancer Immunity and Immunotherapy
text:
ADAR1 is poorly defined in the context of cancer immunity and immunotherapy. We will explore the regulation,
mechanism, and role of ADAR1 in the tumor microenvironment. The proposal will provide an opportunity to
take our understanding of ADAR1 to a new level of mechanism and application.

title: MRI Bone Texture: A Novel Biomarker for Assessment of Bone Quality and Prediction of Complications in Patients Having Spine Fusion Surgery
text:
The lack of clinically available tools for identification of bone abnormalities in patients who undergo spine fusion
surgery contributes to high rates of complications after surgery. This prospective study will investigate a new
technique, based upon standard clinical MRI scans, to detect abnormal bone in patients before surgery, monitor
changes in bone and predict complications that occur after surgery. The long-term goals of our research are to
improve identification of patients at high risk for complications after surgery and provide knowledge that will help
plan follow-up treatment studies.

title: Understanding and Mitigating Vascular Side-Effects Associated with Anti-Amyloid Immunotherapy
text:
Recent FDA accelerated approvals of aducanumab and lecanemab for early-stage Alzheimer’s disease, and
reported positive phase 3 results from donaneab, provide the first disease-modifying treatments to date, albeit
with modest-to-moderate slowing of cognitive decline and the presence of potentially fatal vascular side effects
known as Amyloid-Related Imaging Abnormalities (ARIA) in a subset of treated patients. Here, we will test our
hypothesis that anti-amyloid antibodies with higher binding affinities for vascular amyloid are more likely to cause
ARIA by comparing the biological and pathological binding characteristics of 4 clinical anti-amyloid antibodies to
parenchymal plaque and vascular amyloid in human AD brain tissues and staining in amyloid mouse models. In
addition, we will compare in vivo the ability of the murine analogs of 3 of the anti-amyloid antibodies to both lower
plaque and vascular amyloid burden and induce ARIA in 5XE4 mice and, test antibody cocktails containing an
anti-amyloid antibodies and either an anti-APOE mAb or an anti-complement C1s1 antibody to mitigate ARIA.

title: Identifying drivers of periductal fibrosis in primary sclerosing cholangitis using single-cell analysis of patient biospecimens
text:
Primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC) is a chronic inflammatory condition of the biliary epithelium and a
clinically relevant cause of liver transplantation in the United States. This proposal aims to characterize cellular
drivers of periductal fibrosis, a characteristic histopathologic finding in PSC, using single-cell analyses of
patient tissue and macrophage-fibroblast co-culture studies. This work will dissect the cellular heterogeneity of
the periductal niche and characterize the cell subpopulations that mediate periductal fibrosis, which will
promote the development of more effective diagnostics and therapeutics for PSC patient care.

title: The Role of Copper in Choroid Plexus
text:
PROJECT NARATIVE
This project will generate new information about copper entry into the developing and adult mammalian brain
and determine the role that the blood-cerebrospinal barrier plays in Wilson disease neuropathology. This
information will facilitate understanding of Wilson disease and other disorders associated with copper
misbalance, including Menkes disease, Alzheimer’s disease and Parkinson’s disease.

title: Targeting fibroblast growth factor receptors in cystic fibrosis-associated airway inflammation and mucociliary dysfunction
text:
Cystic fibrosis (CF) and its comorbidities have a major impact on human health and socioeconomic burden,
making the proposed research relevant to public health. CF-associated lung disease is associated with airway
inflammation and mucociliary dysfunction. We will study Fibroblast Growth Factor receptor inhibition as a
potential novel anti-inflammatory therapy option, which is relevant to the NHLBI’s mission to promote the
prevention and treatment of lung diseases and enhance the health of individuals so that they can live longer and
more fulfilling lives.

title: Project 2: High Resolution Mutation Spectra and Multi-Omics for Deducing Etiology and Predicting Disease
text:
Human health is impacted by environmental factors. Genetic changes and cell signaling disruptions 
produced by environmental chemicals underlie many disease outcomes. Given that carcinogenic 
chemicals were released from prior industrial activities at Superfund sites, this project uses a 
systems- based approach to examine the impact of these toxicants on the human genome and the 
repertoire of proteins that are involved in critical signaling systems.

title: Meningeal ectopic lymphoid tissues (mELTs): Composition, organization and expression revealed by imaging and in situ transcriptomics
text:
Multiple sclerosis (MS) remains an insidious disease, with unpredictable outcomes. Though the typical form
of the disease, in which there are relapses and remissions, is responsive to many new medications, ultimately
nearly seventy percent of patients go onto a secondary progressive phase for which there is currently no effective
treatment. This application details experiments to understand the make-up and function of particular structures
that appear in the brain and spinal cord uniquely during this progressive phase – meningeal ectopic lymphoid
tissues (mELTs) – potentially highlighting new therapeutic treatments for progressive MS.

title: Non-contrast 3D T1p Mapping for Myocardial Fibrosis Quantification of Pediatric Cardiomyopathy Patients
text:
Measuring myocardial fibrosis is important for evaluating numerous pediatric
cardiomyopathies, but current cardiac magnetic resonance imaging techniques are not optimal
as they require the use of a contrast agent, general anesthesia, and have limited spatial coverage.
Therefore, we propose developing 3D T1ρ mapping as a non-contrast, free-breathing, whole-
heart myocardial fibrosis imaging technique. This study will establish 3D T1ρ mapping as a useful
imaging test by using deep learning reconstruction and automated data analysis for rapid clinical
translation and evaluation in a large, diverse pediatric patient population.

title: Tranq Burn: the acidity of xylazine and fentanyl combinations
text:
The introduction of xylazine into US street opioids is the most recent large-scale transformation
of the unregulated drug supply. Particularly concerning related to the emergence of xylazine is
the development of severe and persistent skin and soft tissue wounds among people using this
drug. It remains unclear what is causing these wounds, and this project will explore the possibility
that acidity may contribute to their formation.

title: Characterizing gastrointestinal disorder trajectories for autistic sub-groups: Machine learning prediction of risk profiles and response to treatment
text: Gastrointestinal (GI) problems are among the most common concern reported by families of autistic children and youth, but efforts to understand the nuances of GI symptoms are stymied by a lack of longitudinal research using real-world clinical datasets. We will use a multimethod, participatory approach to: (1) qualitatively describe autistic people’s GI experiences throughout the lifespan; (2) quantitatively characterize GI symptom rates, presentations, trajectories, and responses to treatment among autistic children/youth using electronic health records (EHRs) from Children’s Hospital Los Angeles (CHLA) (with both structured data, e.g., diagnosis codes and prescriptions; and unstructured data, i.e., keywords extracted from clinical notes via natural language processing); and (3) build predictive models of risk of GI symptom profiles and response to treatment using both traditional and machine learning approaches. By using longitudinal analyses and real-world clinical data, the proposed study provides a more nuanced prediction of GI symptom profiles and response to treatment, and holds promise for informing future targeted interventions to improve care for autistic individuals.

title: Harnessing activated CD4 T cells to define new mechanisms of protection in tuberculosis
text:
Tuberculosis remains a leading infectious cause of death worldwide, partly due to the lack of an effective vaccine
to prevent disease and the lengthy antibiotic treatment courses needed to cure it. The work proposed here is
expected to address these obstacles by generating new fundamental information about the population of CD4 T
cells that become activated at the site of Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection and by testing the potential of a
new immunotherapeutic strategy that harnesses their protective benefit.

title: Low Density Neutrophils Link Inflammation and Coagulopathy in COVID-19
text:
Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) causes COVID-19 and has resulted in
ongoing pandemic, tragic loss of life, and dire economic consequences. COVID-19 patients with severe
and critical disease also develop pulmonary inflammation and abnormal bleeding problems. We propose
to study the mechanisms underlying these problems and develop a novel therapeutic approach; this will
help us achieve rapid progress toward overcoming the challenges of COVID-19.

title: Membrane compartmentalization in photoreceptor health and disease
text:
In our eyes, there are special cells called photoreceptor neurons that help us see. We want to
understand why proteins in the photoreceptor neurons get misplaced and cause blindness, as well as study
how the different parts of the cells are organized and supported by a structure called the cytoskeleton.

title: Single chromatin fiber multiomics in opioid use disorder brain
text:
The goal of this proposal is to map in 250 brain specimens, including from donors diagnosed
with opioid use disorder, and in the cell culture model, genomic organization and function with
advanced technologies to gain deep insights into molecular mechanisms of drug dependence
and addiction.

title: Precision Medicine in Sepsis with Critical Illness
text:
Sepsis is a highly heterogeneity condition that is common and deadly, and that lacks specific therapies;
however, our groups has described a novel biological approach of categorizing sepsis through two distinct
molecular phenotypes. In this proposal, using deep immunological, microbial, and metabolic measurements,
integrated with cutting edge data science approaches and statistical modelling, we will characterise the
biological basis of the phenotypes, describe treatable pathways and novel therapies, and identify novel
subgroups within the two phenotypes. As trials targeting these phenotypes are about to begin, our studies will
inform them, helping deliver more precise care in sepsis and improve outcomes.

title: Novel Optical Diagnostics with Optical Coherence Tomography
text:
Age-related macular degeneration (AMD) is a leading cause of vision loss, yet detecting and studying its early
vascular and structural changes in vivo remains challenging. This research will develop and apply next-
generation optical coherence tomography (OCT) and OCT angiography (OCTA) to identify imaging biomarkers
predictive of AMD progression, improving early detection and risk stratification. By enabling more precise disease
monitoring, this study aims to facilitate targeted interventions and ultimately reduce AMD-related vision loss.

title: Investigating Neuroprotective Roles of BCAT1 During Hypoxia
text:
Preliminary work from our group has revealed that neuronal BCAA metabolism is disrupted by prenatal hypoxia.
This project aims to characterize hypoxia’s effects on BCAA metabolism, epigenetic signatures, and oxidative
stress, focusing on the role of branched chain amino acid transaminase 1 (BCAT1). Elucidating the function of
BCAT1 in the neuronal hypoxic response will provide insights into the role of BCAA metabolism in the cellular
hypoxic response and will provide crucial insight into the therapeutic potential for supplementation or restriction
of BCAA content in infant formula for prenatal hypoxia.
